articles.title: The Boox Palma 2 Pro finally got me to stop reading on my phone | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The $400 Boox Palma 2 Pro is a smartphone-sized e-reader designed for people who want to read books, articles, and documents on a small E Ink display.
articles.body:
The $400 Boox Palma 2 Pro is a smartphone-sized e-reader designed for people who want to read books, articles, and documents on a small E Ink display. However, it offers more than just a dedicated reading experience because it runs Android and supports Google Play, giving you access to third-party apps. Think of it as a cross between a Kindle and a compact Android tablet.

What drew me to reviewing the Palma 2 Pro was its size. When I’m not reading a physical book, I like to lie on my side and read at night before bed. Most e-readers are squarish and hard to hold without something like a PopSocket, and they can feel too big for reading while lying down. So even though I own a Kindle, I often ended up reading on my iPhone simply because it was more comfortable in my hand. But, reading on your phone for too long can of course cause eye strain. The Palma 2 Pro ultimately solved this problem for me during the two months I spent testing it.

The device’s front-lit screen lets you choose between cool and warm lighting. This was a big plus for me because when I’m reading in bed at night, I don’t want to disturb my sleeping husband with the light. While you can lower the brightness on a smartphone, the Palma 2 Pro can be dimmed to an exceptionally low level. Even when reading in complete darkness, I could see the screen clearly without straining my eyes or disturbing my husband.

Not only was the Boox Palma 2 Pro easier on my eyes, but it was also noticeably lighter than my iPhone, weighing just 175 grams and making it even more comfortable to hold.

And since it’s pocket-sized, I ended up carrying it everywhere, from the doctor’s office to the airport, especially since it fits in my small, everyday purse that isn’t big enough for a Kindle. So, in moments when I would normally scroll on my phone, I was getting some reading in instead.

Since it’s not a locked-down e-reader, you can download apps like Kindle, Kobo, and Libby, as well as apps for audiobooks, podcasts, read-it-later services, and email. This means that you don’t have to use the built-in reader app, and can choose to read on your preferred app.

Access to apps turns the compact E Ink device into a versatile tool for reading, research, and productivity. It’s worth noting that while scrolling through these apps, animations and some interfaces may feel sluggish because not all apps are optimized for E Ink. And while the device is capable of displaying color, images will definitely look less vibrant than they would a smartphone screen.

For me, the Palma 2 Pro became a dedicated device for reading and listening to audiobooks, which allowed me to enjoy the best of both worlds without the usual distractions that come with a smartphone.

The Boox Palma 2 Pro also features a rear camera for scanning documents, a built-in speaker for listening to audio without headphones, and a hybrid SIM slot for cellular data on the go.

The device is compatible with a stylus, so you can take notes and mark up PDFs. However, I can’t speak to that experience since I didn’t receive a stylus with my review unit.

As for battery life, the device lasted about 5–7 days, which worked for me but could be a downside for people who are used to Kindles, which can last for weeks on a single charge. Additionally, if you want to get more juice out of the device, you can just turn off Wi-Fi.

One downside I found, especially for an e-reader at this price point, is that there’s quite a bit of ghosting. Text from a previous page can linger on the screen when you turn to the next page or return to the home screen. There’s a refresh button in the navigation bar that quickly clears it, but it may get annoying for some users to repeatedly have to do that.

I think the Boox Palma 2 Pro is a great device for a very specific type of reader: someone who wants a smartphone-sized device for comfort, portability, as well as access to apps. If you’re someone who loves your Kindle, I don’t think this device is for you. But if, like me, you’re tired of reading on your phone and dealing with eye strain or headaches, the Boox Palma 2 Pro is a great option.

Of course, the price is quite steep for an e-reader, so you’ll have to decide whether the added versatility and portability are worth the extra cost. It’s worth mentioning that Boox is launching a non-Pro Palma 3 soon for $340 that features a black and white display and replaces the Palma 2.

articles.title: What to expect from Apple’s ‘Pro and tell’ event
articles.summary: Apple’s long-rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro, an OLED iPad Mini, and more.
articles.body: It feels like Apple’s Welcome Home event just happened. And the iPhone Duo announcement isn’t all that far in our rearview mirror, either. Yet, the company is back with another launch, focused on the MacBook Pro, it looks like. Its “Pro and tell” event is scheduled for October 28th at 1PM ET in Los Angeles. While obviously nothing is confirmed yet, it sure seems like we’re finally going to get that long-rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro. Beyond that? There could be an OLED update for the iPad Mini, plus M6 updates across other devices, following the M6 debut with the Mac Mini in August. A touchscreen MacBook Pro A MacBook Pro with an OLED touchscreen has been a fixture of the rumor mill since at least early 2023. But now, in late 2026, it may finally come to fruition. The name MacBook Ultra has been floating around, but Apple is unlikely to rebrand its flagship laptop line. This will be the first touchscreen laptop and the first OLED laptop from Apple. It will supposedly feature an iPhone-esque Dynamic Island, but don’t expect a dramatic revamp of the macOS interface — The touchscreen MacBook isn’t going to be some sort of iPad hybrid. It may include a few flourishes, like a magnification effect when you touch the screen or new gesture controls in native apps. But that’s it. It’s also going to stick with the M5 series of chips for the time being — specifically, the M5 Pro and M5 Max. There might not be an M6 Pro or Max, even. Instead, Apple may wait to upgrade its higher-end processors until it introduces the M7 next year. M6 MacBook Pro That doesn’t mean there won’t be an M6 MacBook Pro, however. The base model of the MacBook Pro could be getting a bump from the M5 after the M6 debuted in the Mac Mini earlier this year. It might also get a slight redesign, including a hole-punch style camera. Unfortunately, they’re also expected to come with a price increase as component shortages reverberate through the Apple lineup. M6 iMac The iMac is also expected to get an M6 update, nearly two years after its last revision. Apple’s all-in-one desktop appears like it’s going to skip right over the M5. Don’t expect any real changes beyond that, though. But at least we might get some new color options, just like we did with the M4 model. OLED iPad Mini Another long-rumored device that might finally be making its debut on Wednesday is the OLED iPad Mini. Other than the iPad Pro, the tablet lineup has stuck with LCDs until now. The new OLED iPad could kick off a broader transition for the product line. The screen upgrade may add $100 to the cost, though. Otherwise, it likely won’t be a significant redesign, but expect a processor upgrade from the aging A17 to the A20 that debuted with the iPhone 18.

articles.body: ‘The Real Housewives of Atlanta’ star Pinky Cole is facing another financial hurdle, as a finance company has asked a bankruptcy judge for permission to pursue remedies that could lead to the foreclosure of one of her rental properties in Georgia. The development comes amid her ongoing bankruptcy proceedings and months after reports of a creditor attempting to seize another property she owns.According to documents obtained by TMZ, Selene Finance LP filed a motion in Cole’s bankruptcy case on Thursday, claiming that she owes more than $164,000 on a three-bedroom, two-bathroom home in the Atlanta area.Finance company alleges mortgage payments have been missed since December 2025In its filing, Selene Finance LP alleged that Cole had not made mortgage payments on the property since December 2025. articles.title: Sylvester Stallone On Casting Daughter In ‘Tulsa King’: “Of Course It’s Nepotism, You Idiot”
articles.summary: An interview with Sylvester Stallone from October 16 is going viral thanks to some candid comments the Tulsa King actor made about the casting of his daughte...
articles.body:
An interview with Sylvester Stallone from October 16 is going viral thanks to some candid comments the Tulsa King actor made about the casting of his daughter Scarlet Rose Stallone.

Stallone has a blunt message to naysayers: "Of course it's nepotism, you idiot."

The subject came up as Stallone was reflecting on comments he's heard about the casting. "First they go, 'Nepotism is terrible,'" he told USA Today . "I said, 'Oh please, you're not a good parent if you haven't performed a little nepotism. Then obviously you don't care about your kids, because they come first.'"

Stallone added, "'Of course it's nepotism, you idiot. That's why we're parents. We want the best for our children. So obviously, we let them have every advantage.'"

The "nepo baby" charge has increased in visibility in recent years, as the offspring of Hollywood celebrities grow in prominence. Ryan Murphy alone has provided a home base for many: Billie Lourd (Carrie Fisher), Emma Roberts (Erik Roberts), Lily Rabe (Jill Clayburgh), Kaia Gerber (Cindy Crawford), Charlie Hall (Julia Louis-Dreyfus), Homer Gere (Richard Gere) and Ella Beatty (Annette Bening and Warren Beatty) have all featured in various Murphy series.

Stallone, though, points out that parents can only do so much. "Can they maintain that level of excellence?," he asks in the USA Today article. "That's out of our hands. But if you can open the door, we'll see if they have the ability to go through it.

"People will say, 'She got that job, it's too easy.' You're right. Perhaps it could be. But to maintain that, to be in front of millions of people, you either got it or you don't."

articles.title: The hottest AI wearables and gadgets you should know about
articles.summary: We compiled a list of all the hottest AI wearables, including Muse Charm, Bee, Friend, Plaud, and more.
articles.body:
A slew of AI-powered gadgets on the market aims to integrate artificial intelligence into our daily lives like never before.

Some of these AI wearables — including necklaces, rings, and wristbands, as well as portable devices — serve as productivity tools, while others claim to act as friendly companions listening to your everyday thoughts. Even OpenAI is working on a compact AI companion device.

Below, we’ve rounded up some of the most notable devices.

Bee is an affordable pendant priced at $49.99 that can either be clipped to your clothing or worn like a fitness band. This device records everything it hears and learns your routines and preferences to create reminders and notes for you. It even features a mute button for those times you want some privacy.

The companion app (currently available only on iOS) is included with a $19 monthly subscription. The app allows you to interact with Bee directly and ask it questions. You can also get key takeaways from your day and chronological transcripts of your conversations.

Amazon acquired the wearables startup in July 2025, launching its first new products earlier this month.

Amazon introduced two new devices: the Bee Frontier, priced at $74.99, which can be worn on the wrist or clipped to clothing, and the Bee Eclipse, priced at $99.99, a credit-card-sized device that attaches magnetically to the back of a smartphone.

Both offer the same core functionality as the previous generation, positioning Bee as a more affordable alternative to AI devices such as the Plaud Note and Plaud NotePin. Users can also choose to connect Bee to Alexa.

Friend is one of the most hyped entrants in the “personal AI” device market.

This $129 white pendant hangs around your neck and functions as an emotional support companion. It recognizes your tone and mood, allowing you to chat with it as if it were a friend. It connects to your phone via Bluetooth and constantly listens, ready to respond or send you proactive messages, like wishing you good luck before an interview.

However, it has also faced criticism, including backlash against its subway ad campaign in NYC. People vandalized the ads, writing messages like “surveillance capitalism.”

Likely as an attempt to stay relevant, the company recently unveiled a major product update, introducing a new voice feature. Under the name “Friend 2.0,” the updated device includes a built-in speaker that allows it to communicate with users and express a more distinctive personality.

Formerly known as Rewind, Limitless is another conversation-recording pendant priced at $99.

This device continuously listens, transcribing meetings, calls, and conversations (with consent) into searchable and summarized knowledge. It’s ideal for professionals, especially journalists, looking to recall important discussions.

The companion app comes with 10 hours of AI features per month — such as transcription and summaries — with the option to unlock unlimited features for $29 per month.

Meta introduced its first AI wearable in September, offering a new way for users to access its personal AI assistant, Muse.

The device has not yet shipped, but it is expected to feature Jolly, a playful digital avatar that represents the AI assistant. Housed in a pocket-sized device that can be carried around or attached to a keychain, the wearable includes a miniature display showing the avatar. Users will be able to interact with Muse through voice commands and have it complete tasks for them.

Nirva is a startup founded by former Meta Reality Labs employees, building an AI wearable focused on personal growth rather than productivity or meeting notes.

Worn as a pendant or bracelet, the device listens to the wearer’s speech and uses AI to turn everyday experiences into a personal journal, helping users better understand their emotions, communication style, and habits. Through its companion app, users can explore patterns in their behavior, gain insights into how they communicate, and find ways to improve.

Nirva plans to open orders in November, with shipments to early users targeted for the end of the year. The device will cost $249.

Priced at $89, this device can answer your questions, summarize your conversations, create to-do lists, and help schedule meetings. Additionally, Omi is constantly listening and running your conversations through ChatGPT, allowing it to remember the context about you and offer personalized advice.

Omi can be worn as a necklace, but another notable aspect is that it can be attached to the side of your head with medical tape and can detect when you’re speaking to it.

At $159, Plaud’s NotePin is one of the pricier options on this list; however, its built-in AI transcription and summarization features make it a valuable tool for lawyers, journalists, and students attending meetings or lectures.

The tiny wearable voice recorder can be worn on your wrist or attached magnetically to your clothing. The recordings are saved in real time on your phone, eliminating the hassle of manual note-taking. The device includes 300 free monthly transcription minutes, but with the $8.33 per month Pro plan, you upgrade your transcription time to 1,200 minutes.

This year, the company is gearing up to launch a $179 ultra-thin note-taking device called the Plaud Note Pro , which is now available for preorder.

Rabbit R1 is another AI gadget that has quickly become a topic of interest in the tech world, despite facing some challenges during its initial launch. This small, retro-styled handheld device features a touchscreen and rotating camera, at a price point of $199.

The device is designed to be phone-adjacent, allowing you to perform tasks such as booking flights, ordering meals, and controlling apps without needing to pull out your phone each time. Following a crucial software update that rectified previous performance issues, the Rabbit R1 now boasts expanded AI features. For instance, it introduces “Creations,” a feature that allows you to build your own tools and even games.

Sandbar emerged from stealth last year, unveiling the Stream ring, an AI wearable designed for note-taking.

It features a built-in microphone that remains off by default and can be activated through a flat, touch-sensitive surface on the top of the ring. By pressing and holding the panel, users can record notes, interact with an AI assistant through the companion smartphone app, and manage media playback, including playing, pausing, skipping tracks, and adjusting volume

articles.title: Jessica Biel Says ‘7th Heaven’ Reboot Will ‘Modernize’ the Show Now That TV Has ‘Less Limitations’: ‘We Were Very Careful About What Our Audience Wanted’
articles.summary: Nearly 20 years since the conclusion of “7th Heaven,” and over a year since the news broke about its reboot, original star Jessica Biel is giving fans an upd...
articles.body:
Nearly 20 years since the conclusion of "7th Heaven," and over a year since the news broke about its reboot , original star Jessica Biel is giving fans an update on the new iteration of the show, including how she plans to "modernize" it for today's audience and what she hopes to accomplish on set as a producer.

"What we want to create, how we want to modernize it, is really the things that are happening for teenagers and families that have teenagers all the way down to the youngest child — technology-based issues, school stuff, bullying stuff, drugs, alcohol," Biel said on a recent episode of Collider Ladies Night . "All of those things we want to address in a very real way, which is, I think, what the original kind of gently touched on, but we were very careful about what our audience wanted. We had a lot of limitations. We have less limitations now."

Created by Brenda Hampton and produced by Aaron Spelling, "7th Heaven" debuted on The WB (later The CW) in 1996 and concluded in 2007. The show proved to be a major early hit for the network, ultimately airing for 11 seasons and nearly 250 episodes. The show followed the Camden family and their seven children in the fictional town of Glen Oak, Calif., where Eric was a Protestant minister. In addition to Biel, the cast also included Stephen Collins, Catherine Hicks, Barry Watson, David Gallagher, Beverley Mitchell, Mackenzie Rosman, Nikolas Brino, and Lorenzo Brino.

When asked if the original show could withstand the test of time, Biel explained that the core theme — family — was "what was working back then." "I'm looking for what I can watch with my kids on television. It's limited. I cannot watch a lot of these things with them, and they love TV, and it's my business. My husband and I are in this business together doing these things, and we can't share a lot of that with our kids," she continued. "So, I think the idea of whatever faith you want to have, that's important. That we don't have a lot on television, whether you believe that or go down that road or not. There are a lot of people that really do want to walk down that road, so I think some kind of faith, some kind of family, community, and maybe something not so jaded, like something a little bit more glass-half-full. It's not that it's soft, because it's realistic."

As a producer, Biel plans to create a "safe place for people to be really creative and really vulnerable," she explained.

"When I'm on set as a producer, I'm always thinking about the safety net of the set and the communication that you hope you can have — free-flowing communication with your actors and your crew," she added. "You just want to create a safe place for people to be really creative and really vulnerable, because a lot of the stuff that I'm doing now, the content that I'm doing now, it's emotional stuff. It's people really putting themselves out there on the chopping block emotionally, and if you don't have that space protected, I think it's hard. It's hard to give those kinds of performances."

Variety exclusively broke the news of the "7th Heaven" reboot back in May 2025. At the time, sources said that the new iteration of the show would focus on a diverse family, and that none of the original cast members would appear.

articles.title: iFixit’s look inside the iPhone Duo may explain those broken screens and hinges
articles.summary: The iPhone Duo is the most repairable foldable yet, but that’s not saying much.
articles.body: As is tradition, iFixit has torn open the latest iPhone and laid its parts bare on a table. It found some interesting details about how Apple might be hiding the crease on the Duo’s folding screen and gave it a 5/10 repairability score. That might not seem particularly high, but it’s the best score the site has given to a foldable yet. The internal screen’s matte nano-texture cover doesn’t just make it more readable in bright sunlight; it also helps mask the crease by scattering reflections. When looking at the display under a microscope, iFixit also found oval-shaped subpixels arranged at various angles, which the site believes are designed to reduce artifacts and further mask the crease down the middle of the display. [Media: The nano-texture outer layer is relatively easy to replace without swapping out the OLED underneath. If you do need to repair the display itself, however, good luck. As is the case with other foldables, it’s an expensive nightmare. Dust did make it into the USB-C port, speaker grills, and the hinge — making it a bit crunchy. But noticeably less of the glow dust found its way inside the phone than the Z Fold8 or Pixel 11 Pro Fold. As for reports of damaged screens and cracking hinges, iFixit has some theories. The hinge on the iPhone Duo is incredibly complex, and they suspect part of it sometimes isn’t descending properly. There is also an accordion cable that passes over that exact spot, and it’s near the edge of the battery. It’s possible this is concentrating pressure and leading to the “audible crack” reported by some and the broken screens. Apple did not immediately return a request for comment.

articles.title: Eric Bauza Dies: Emmy-Winning Voice Of Bugs Bunny & Daffy Duck & Much More Was 46
articles.summary: “He followed in the footsteps of giants like Mel Blanc.” So said Channing Dungey, Chairman, Warner Bros. Television Group and US Networks tonight after the f...
articles.body:
"He followed in the footsteps of giants like Mel Blanc."

So said Channing Dungey, Chairman, Warner Bros. Television Group and US Networks tonight after the family of Eric Bauza announced the death of the most recent voice actor behind characters like Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, including in this year's much-loved Coyote vs. Acme . Bauza was 46.

Filling the shoes of the legendary Mel Blanc at Looney Tunes was no small task, but the three-time Emmy winner did so capably for years. Dungey called Bauza an "incredible talent."

Besides the two biggies, other Looney Tunes characters he brought to life included Tweety, Foghorn Leghorn, Pepé Le Pew, Porky Pig, Road Runner, Elmer Fudd and Marvin the Martian. He voiced many of those characters in Space Jam: A New Legacy and Looney Tunes Cartoons . For the latter, Bauza in 2022 won the first ever Children's and Family Emmy Award for Outstanding Voice Performance in an Animated Program. That was for Looney Tunes Cartoons . He won the award again for Teen Titans Go! in 2024. In 2023, he won the Outstanding Voice Performance in a Preschool Program Emmy for Bugs Bunny Builders .

Here's a bit of Buaza and fellow Emmy winner Peter Cullen both doing voices at the ceremony in 2023.

That alone would have been a career, but Bauza also voiced Stimpy, the animated Luke Skywalker, Puss in Boots, Bam-Bam Rubble, Donatello, Leonardo, the animated Jason Bourne, Robert "Big Bob" Belcher, Jimmy Pesto, Sr., Woody Woodpecker, Two-Face, Bane, Jimmy Olsen and Aquaman.

A partial list of the other projects to which he lent his talents includes The Super Mario Bros. Movie, Avatar: The Last Airbender series, The Fairly OddParents, Phineas and Ferb, Rick and Morty, Ultimate Spider-Man, Teen Titans Go!, The Tom and Jerry Show, The Mr. Peabody & Sherman Show, Lego Star Wars, Transformers: Robots in Disguise, SpongeBob SquarePants, The Powerpuff Girls, Muppet Babies, Star Trek: Lower Decks, Krapopolis and X-Men '97 .

"Eric Bauza was a unique voice talent who brought joy and laughter to millions around the world," said Warner Bros. Animation and Warner Bros. Pictures Animation in a joint statement. "During his 15 years at Warner Bros. Animation, he was the voice of Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck among countless other characters. He followed in the footsteps of giants like Mel Blanc. Eric said that carrying on the legendary legacy of the Looney Tunes was among the greatest honors of his life. In addition to his incredible talent, Eric was a treasured part of our animation family. Our hearts go out to his loved ones."

articles.title: Man bought Samsung Z Flip6 for Rs 1.1 lakh, but screen went black during warranty; consumer commission finds deficiency in service, orders Rs 98,000 payout plus 9% interest on refund
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A consumer commission in Haryana has directed Samsung India to refund Rs 88,000 for a Z Flip6 phone that developed problems during the warranty
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A consumer commission in Haryana has directed Samsung India to refund Rs 88,000 for a Z Flip6 phone that developed problems during the warranty period, after the company failed to establish that physical damage caused the defect. The commission also ordered the company to pay Rs 5,000 as compensation for mental agony and harassment and Rs 5,000 towards litigation costs.Samsung Z Flip6 develops heating and display problemsAccording to the commission order, Vicky Kapoor, the complainant, purchased a Samsung Z Flip6 from Guru Simran Mobile in Rohtak on December 18, 2024, for Rs 1,09,999.Within a few days of the purchase, the phone allegedly began heating up and experiencing network drops during calls. The complainant approached Samsung's authorised service centre, in the last week of January 2025. Technician at the centre reset the phone but did not prepare a job sheet, and assured him that the problem would be resolved.The same problems reportedly returned in March 2025 and the service centre again reset the device. Kapoor alleged that this reset of the phone resulted in the loss of his phone data.On July 28, 2025, the phone heated up during a call and its screen went black. The complainant gave the device at the service centre. The job sheet issued that day recorded the phone's warranty status as “full warranty” and described the problem as “display not working, black display”.When he visited the service centre the following day, he was told that the repair would cost Rs 45,000, according to the complaint. Kapoor allegedly asked them to repair the phone under warranty, but the service centre refused.Samsung disputed the allegations, contending that the phone had dents on its hinge and scratches on the screen, causing damage to the display. It argued that the damage resulted from mishandling by the customer and made the phone ineligible for warranty repairs.The company also alleged that a repair estimate had been provided and added that the phone was outside the standard warranty because of physical damage.Kapoor sought a refund of Rs 1,09,999 with interest, Rs 50,000 in compensation for mental harassment and Rs 11,000 towards litigation expenses from the commission.Commission's finding on warranty disputeThe bench comprising president Nagender Singh Kadian and members Dr Tripti Pannu and Dr Vijender Singh, examined the purchase invoice, service records, photographs and other documents submitted from both the sides.It noted that the first job sheet, issued on July 28, 2025, recorded the phone as being under warranty, however, a subsequent job sheet dated August 26, 2025, classified the phone as being out of warranty.The commission found that Samsung had not produced reliable evidence explaining the change in warranty status."The opposite parties have not placed on record any cogent and reliable evidence to explain the change in the warranty status from ‘Full Warranty’ to ‘Out of Warranty’," the bench said.On the company's claim that physical damage had caused the defect, the commission said that this claim has not been supported by any solid report or evidence.It also examined the photographs submitted by Samsung but found them insufficient to establish that the customer was responsible for the damage."In the absence of such technical evidence, the contention of the opposite parties that the defect was caused by physical damage cannot be accepted merely on the basis of the photographs placed on record," the order noted.It then held that the phone had developed a defect during the warranty period and that the opposite parties had failed to provide the required repair or replacement under the warranty. It found deficiency in service on their part.Considering that the phone had been used for more than seven months, the commission directed Samsung, as the manufacturer, to refund the purchase price after deducting 20 percent towards depreciation."Accordingly, there is deficiency in service on the part of the opposite parties. Opposite party No. 1, being the manufacturer of the mobile phone, is liable to refund the purchase price after deducting 20 percent towards depreciation, considering that the complainant used the mobile phone for more than seven months," the commission concluded.Final orderThe Rohtak District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission allowed the complaint and directed Samsung India Electronics to:Refund Rs 88,000 after deducting 20 percent depreciation from the original purchase price of Rs 1,09,999.Pay 9 percent annual interest on the refund from August 22, 2025, the date the complaint was filed, until realisation.Pay Rs 5,000 as compensation for mental agony and harassment.Pay Rs 5,000 towards litigation expenses.The company was directed to comply within 30 days of receiving a copy of the order. The commission noted that the phone was already in the possession of the service centre.The fixed payout ordered, excluding interest, is Rs 98,000. The commission did not order a refund of the full purchase price or award the entire compensation and litigation expenses sought by the complainant.

articles.title: Apple updates the iPad Mini with a larger OLED display
articles.summary: Apple has announced an upgraded iPad Mini with a larger 8.5-inch OLED display. It starts at $699 with Wi-Fi-only.
articles.body: Apple announced a new iPad Mini with a larger, 8.5-inch OLED display. The company revealed the new device just days before its “Pro and tell” event on Wednesday. The iPad Mini starts at $699 for the Wi-Fi-only model, and $849 for Wi-Fi and cellular. At 5.4mm thick, the iPad Mini is thinner and lighter than its predecessor. It also has bezels that are 24 percent slimmer. This allows the device to maintain the same small form factor with a display that’s slightly larger than the previous generation’s 8.3-inch screen. The iPad Mini offers a peak brightness of up to 1,200 nits, along with a 1-nit minimum brightness that could make it easier on the eyes in dim lighting. The new device still doesn’t come with Apple’s ProMotion technology for smoother scrolling, as the technical specs say it supports up to 4K resolution at a 60Hz refresh rate. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Aside from an OLED display, the new iPad Mini features an upgraded A20 Pro chip capable of running on-device AI models. This enables support for some of Apple’s new Siri AI features, including the ability to tweak the expressiveness and pace of the assistant’s voice. Although models with 128GB or 256GB of storage come with a five-core CPU with two super cores and three efficiency cores, the 512GB model offers a six-core CPU with two super cores and four efficiency cores. All models come with a 16-core Neural Engine. Additionally, Apple says the iPad Mini comes with a new “Acoustic Display,” which it describes as including “specially designed woofers” that are “paired through the display to produce punchier bass and more volume.” It also has custom tweeters between the device’s glass and aluminum enclosure “for clearer highs.” Some other updates include a 12MP front-facing camera that’s now on the long edge of the iPad Mini, making it easier for video calls in landscape orientation. It has an IP67 rating for protection against water and dust, in addition to Apple’s next-gen C2 cellular modem and in-house N1 networking chip. Apple promises up to 10 hours of battery life when watching videos or browsing the web on Wi-Fi. [Image: The iPad Mini has a Super Retina XDR display. This new iPad Mini follows Apple’s seventh-generation version released in 2024, which arrived three years after the sixth-generation model in 2021. That seventh-generation iPad Mini, which started at $499, was primarily a spec bump, with the A17 Pro chip, support for the Apple Pencil Pro, and an upgrade to 128GB base storage. In his review, David Pierce called it a “new low for the product” that “feels like an iPad designed by a supply chain, not by someone who actually wants you to like the product.” The upgraded iPad Mini comes ahead of a string of other rumored product launches that could take place this week, which could include a touchscreen MacBook Pro, along with an M6-equipped MacBook Pro and iMac. Preorders for the new iPad Mini start on Wednesday, October 28th, with availability on November 6th. The iPad Mini is available in “midnight” and “starlight” colors, along with 128GB, 256GB, and 512GB configurations. There’s a glare-reducing nano-texture display option for the 256GB and 512GB models as well.

articles.title: Apple unveils new iPad mini with OLED display and faster A20 Pro chip | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The new iPad mini features a thinner and lighter design than its predecessor.
articles.body:
Apple on Monday announced a new iPad mini with a larger 8.5-inch OLED display. The tablet features a thinner and lighter design than its predecessor and is powered by an A20 Pro chip. The new iPad mini starts at $699 for the Wi-Fi model and $849 for the Wi-Fi and cellular model. The tech giant revealed the new device just days before its “Pro and Tell” event that’s scheduled to take place on Wednesday.

The new iPad mini is 5.4 mm in thickness, and available in two colors.

The device delivers peak brightness of up to 1,200 nits, more than twice that of the previous generation device, along with full screen brightness of 600 nits for SDR and HDR content and a 2 million:1 contrast ratio. Apple says the iPad mini is ideal for dim-light environments.

The iPad mini also comes with a new nano-texture display option that reduces glare in bright environments, a feature already available on the iPad Pro. The updated tablet now also features a 12-megapixel center stage front camera, faster wireless and cellular connectivity, and fast-charge support.

The Super Retina XDR display uses OLED technology for pixel-level lighting control, delivering deeper blacks, richer contrast, and support for the P3 wide color gamut for more vibrant colors.

It also features an “Acoustic Display” that Apple says enhances the audio experience when gaming, watching videos, or editing content. Specially designed woofers integrated into the display deliver deeper bass and higher volume for richer sound, per the company.

The new iPad mini launches with the next generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, which can draw on a user’s personal context to help them find what they need, answer questions, and understand what’s on their screen.

Powered by a 7 core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each core, the iPad mini has up to 4.5-times faster AI performance than the previous generation, according to Apple. Additionally, The A20 Pro also features a 6 core CPU, delivering up to 60% faster multithreaded performance for everyday tasks such as photo editing and multitasking across apps.

The device can be pre-ordered on October 28, with availability beginning November 6.

articles.body: The Remarkable Paper Pro Move is essentially a digital notepad, with a skinny 7.3-inch E Ink screen that’s easy to hold one-handed to jot down notes or ideas. At $449 new, it’s not exactly cheap, but buying refurbished is a way to save, as always. Remarkable itself offers the refurbished Paper Pro Move for that same price with a polymer Book Folio case and a Marker Plus that has a built-in eraser tool. It comes with a one-year warranty. If you’re alright with trading the one-year warranty for a 90-day one, Woot has the same bundle for about just $342. That offer is available exclusively to new Woot customers, who can enter the code REMARKABLE at checkout to save 10 percent on their order through November 2nd. The deal is good for returning shoppers, too, costing $379.99. [Product: Remarkable Paper Pro Move | The Paper Pro Move makes it easy to convert your handwritten notes to text, and store files on third-party cloud services. You can also view your notes in Remarkable’s apps and screen share from your E Ink device. However, Remarkable’s Connect subscription (a free 50-day trial for new users/devices) and $3.99 per month thereafter offers access to a larger suite of features. With it, you can search your handwritten notes, import docs and articles to the device to mark notes on, get AI-powered summaries of your handwritten text (viewable in a browser), and more. Other great deals to consider * Best Buy is trying to reach more gamers, so it’s dangling a $5 gift card offer for those who sign up for a Best Buy Gamers profile. Beyond being a hub for gaming-centric info, trailers, and polls, it’s a portal for highlighting deals and its upcoming drops, like the Thursday, November 5th midnight in-store launch of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (and the limited edition Nintendo Switch 2 hardware). We last covered this camera a year later when it was discounted to $549.99. The feature-light camera looks like a pricey mirrorless model, but is instead a glorified digital camera that can shoot 18-megapixel shots that evoke the analog era through various modes and filters. Read our hands-on. * I’m still getting used to Belkin being one of the most prolific accessory makers for the Nintendo Switch 2. One of its latest, the Charging Grip, is discounted by $10 at Amazon in the black color. Originally $99.99 for the handheld case that adds some non-slip ergonomics via Joy-Con grips, it’s down to $89.99. Most of the price comes from the 10,000mAh 30W USB-C battery that’s included, which magnetically attaches to the Grip on the back of your console. The Grip allows for the Switch 2’s kickstand to extend, and a big advantage here compared to most third-party console covers is that the case is thin enough to allow for docking with Nintendo’s first-party dock.

articles.title: After multiple partnership projects, Bose acquires US audio brand Skullcandy; CEO Lila Snyder says it will give the company access to…
articles.summary: Bose has acquired American audio brand Skullcandy.
articles.body: ​Bose has acquired American audio brand Skullcandy. The purchase follows a partnership through which Skullcandy released several headphones and earbuds using Bose audio technology. The company has confirmed that Skullcandy will remain a separate brand within Bose’s Premium Consumer Audio business and continue operating from Park City, Utah. However, Bose did not disclose how much it paid for the company, which it acquired from a fund managed by Connecticut-based private investment firm Mill Road Capital Management. The deal adds a younger, generally less expensive audio brand to Bose’s portfolio while extending its reach into communities associated with board sports, music, gaming, and fitness.“Skullcandy gives us access to a customer base that we think we’re largely missing with the Bose brand,” CEO Lila Snyder told Wired. Bose plans to give Skullcandy greater access to its audio technology, business resources, retail relationships, and global distribution network. However, the company said Skullcandy would retain the freedom to develop products that reflect its existing identity and customers.Bose and Skullcandy worked together before the acquisitionThe companies began their product partnership in 2025 with the Method 360 ANC earbuds. Skullcandy designed the earbuds, and Bose supplied and tuned the audio components as part of its Sound by Bose licensing program.Skullcandy followed up in July 2026 with the Crusher 1080 ANC headphones, which combine the company’s adjustable bass system with Bose noise-cancellation and spatial audio technology. At IFA Berlin, Skullcandy also displayed the Noise Master Buds Open.Earlier products let both companies test how Bose technology could work with Skullcandy’s design style and lower pricing before the acquisition.“We believe this is a win for Skullcandy and our fans,” Skullcandy CEO Brian Garofalow said. He added that the deal would bring Bose’s audio expertise and technology into more Skullcandy products.Why Bose wants Skullcandy’s customersBose is known for premium headphones and speakers, including its QuietComfort range. Skullcandy sells products at lower prices and has built its brand around younger buyers and communities connected to skating, snowboarding, gaming and music.Snyder said Skullcandy would remain in Park City because the Utah city is closely linked to boardsports culture. Keeping the company there is meant to preserve its connections with athletes and customers, rather than moving it to Bose’s operations in Massachusetts.“As a privately held company, we have the freedom to make bold, long-term investments in opportunities we believe in, and Skullcandy is a great example of that,” Snyder said in the acquisition statement.Skullcandy is Bose’s third acquisition of 2026Bose bought StreamUnlimited Engineering in June. The Vienna-based company develops software and hardware modules used in streaming and connected audio products. Bose said that the purchase would help place its audio technology in more third-party devices and smart-home systems.On October 1, Bose acquired Firelight Technologies, the Australian company behind FMOD, an audio-software platform used by game developers. Skullcandy is its third acquisition of the year.The company also owns McIntosh and Sonus Faber through its earlier purchase of McIntosh Group. Those brands occupy the high-end audio market, while Skullcandy gives Bose a presence at more accessible prices. The company has not announced any new products resulting from the acquisition yet.​You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Apple acknowledges iPhone Duo display ‘issue’ after reports of cracked screens
articles.summary: Apple says a ‘small number’ of iPhone Duos have shown the cracked inner screen problem and that owners should contact AppleCare.
articles.body: Following reports of iPhone Duos with cracked and broken inside screens, often showing a bright line running from the center to the right side, Apple says in a statement to Bloomberg and 9to5Mac that it’s aware of “an issue impacting the inner display” on a “small number of iPhone Duo units.” If your iPhone Duo is affected, Apple says to contact AppleCare for a replacement. Here is the full statement, which Apple’s Alex Kirschner shared with The Verge: > The response to iPhone Duo from early users has been incredibly positive, and we are seeing exciting things from developers who are rapidly updating their apps to take advantage of its unique form factor. We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units. If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement. Kirshner says most units aren’t susceptible and that the issues appear quickly on units with the defect. Shortly after launch, iPhone Duo users started reporting similar issues where the hinge would tighten, and opening the device caused a crack and the distinctive bright lines on the display. One user in Australia said that an Apple Store replaced their unit “on the spot.” This weekend, iFixit published its teardown of the phone and gave its perspective on why some phones might be cracking. Where the damage has been happening, iFixit shows how the foldable screen might be pushing against a center bar. [Media: The Verge has contacted Apple about the reports, but has not received an on-the-record response about the issues with these new phones. They’re some of the first devices to launch after new CEO John Ternus took over from Tim Cook. Updates, October 26th: Added Apple’s statement and additional context.
